purpose: Close the gap declared in esm3_fibromyalgia_bridge_v1: are the opioid module and the FM-specific ECM genes COL9A1/PTN connected by INDIRECT paths in the STRING network, more closely than chance?
hypothesis: H1: mean shortest-path length from opioid-module genes to {COL9A1, PTN} is SHORTER than in degree-preserving rewired nulls.
null_hypothesis: H0: the observed mean shortest-path length is drawn from the rewired-null distribution.
statistic: mean unweighted shortest-path length over all reachable (source,target) pairs
null_model: degree-preserving double-edge swap (nx.double_edge_swap), nswap = 10 x |E|, N = 1000 permutations, seeded
optional_stopping: PROHIBITED — N=1000 fixed before execution; no re-running with different N
kill_criteria: If p >= 0.05 the parallel-pathway hypothesis is FALSIFIED and every fibromyalgia framing is removed from the ESM3 bridge; ESM3 remains a pure generative-model-vs-noise-floor experiment.
regime: STRING functional network, confidence >= 0.400, human, 49-gene induced subgraph. Claims hold only in this regime.
axis_declaration: Graph-topology axis only. A short path is topological proximity in a curated interaction database — NOT causal evidence in fibromyalgia tissue.

consumers.p_value: decides whether the FM framing survives in esm3_fibromyalgia_bridge_v1
consumers.bridging_nodes: candidate targets for the next STRING/expression query

hash_method: sha256(json.dumps(obj, sort_keys=True, separators=(',',':'), ensure_ascii=False)) computed over the full object EXCLUDING the hash field itself
